passages.text: How the Job Desk works | Ian | DTRT Lab Skip to content Ian | DTRT Lab Job Desk Prices FAQ Get my free office map Job Desk · Episode 1 How the Job Desk works You're on a job. A new lead just texted. Who answers it? Here is one evening at a heating and air company, start to finish, in the Job Desk: the AI office manager I build for small service businesses. Demo, made-up data Every screen below is from the public demo . Pretendwell Heating & Air Co., its customers and its numbers are made up.

passages.title: How the Job Desk works | Ian | DTRT Lab
passages.text: On this page The one-hour gap What the Job Desk is Tonight: the nightly Report Card Needs you: one queue Approve, edit or skip Jobs: one timeline per job Sent log: you approve every send What it never does Who it's for The one-hour gap 17% Only 17% of HVAC companies reply to a new lead within an hour. 78% reply the same day. Source: Jobber, 2026 Home Service Trends Report, via Jobber's HVAC industry trends . Most companies do reply. Just not fast.

passages.title: How the Job Desk works | Ian | DTRT Lab
passages.text: Jobber also notes that customers often reach out to more than one company at once, and the first business to respond often gets the job. When you're on a job all day, the office work waits until night. So what if the office work kept up, and you only touched what needs you? What the Job Desk is Four screens: Tonight, Needs you, Jobs and a sent log. The system drafts each customer message, and you approve, edit or skip it. It goes out only after you approve it.

passages.title: How the Job Desk works | Ian | DTRT Lab
passages.text: Autopilot, which would send without asking, is an opt-in setting, and it's off by default. Tonight: the nightly Report Card Every night, you get one screen on your phone. It sends at 8 PM by default, and you can pick any time. It starts with one line: all clear, or how many things need you. Then at most 3 things, most urgent first, and 4 numbers compared with last week. One line says what you approved and sent today, linked to the full log.

passages.title: How the Job Desk works | Ian | DTRT Lab
passages.text: Urgent pings go to you only, for safety words or a lead waiting over an hour, and never more than 2 a day. Needs you: one queue The order is safety first, then urgent, then money at stake, then what's due. Any lead waiting over 15 minutes counts as urgent and turns red. In the demo, Maria's web form says "No heat, furnace clicks but won't start," and she has waited 48 minutes, so she's first. Approve, edit or skip Edit: change a word or rewrite it. It saves as a draft.

passages.title: How the Job Desk works | Ian | DTRT Lab
passages.text: Approve: only then does it go out, and it leaves the list. (In the demo, nothing is really sent.) Skip: it won't come back tonight. Jobs: one timeline per job Demo, made-up data Every step has a time, and who did it. Jobs shows every job and where it stands. Open one to see what the customer said, what the system drafted, and what you approved and sent. Open quotes get up to 3 drafted nudges, on day 2, day 5 and day 10, and each one goes out only when you approve it. Drafts stop the moment the customer replies.

passages.title: DTRT Afterlight — La isla recuerda
passages.text: English narration renders conversations that often occur in Spanish. Historical and adaptation notes are supplied separately. Cut A transmitter that no longer exists. A workbench lamp left on. Insight Gabriel is introduced by a repair he cannot finish. The story will keep asking what can be restored and what can only be recorded. 1 — The completed journey The radio on Gabriel Vélez’s workbench could receive everything except the station its owner wanted.

passages.title: DTRT Afterlight — La isla recuerda
passages.text: He turned the tuning knob through two sermons, an argument about baseball, and a song his mother used to sing incorrectly. The old woman who owned the set had put a piece of masking tape beside the frequency she preferred. Gabriel had replaced a capacitor and cleaned the contacts. He could restore the machine, but not the transmitter that had stopped broadcasting three months earlier. He was considering how to explain this when his sister called. “What did I break?” Inés asked.

passages.title: DTRT Afterlight — La isla recuerda
passages.text: The shop’s rolling door was halfway down. Beyond it, Solera was still mostly dark. A delivery truck passed with a loose metal panel knocking against its bed. “This week?” “When we were little.” Gabriel set down his soldering iron. He could hear ventilation on her end, a low vibration with something rattling inside it. She was at a work site. She had told him she was taking three days off. “The blue pitcher,” he said. “That’s what we told Mami.” The line made a dry clicking sound. Inés inhaled sharply.

passages.title: DTRT Afterlight — La isla recuerda
passages.text: “If somebody tells you I need rescuing, ask them that. And don’t use—” Her voice stopped. The ventilation stopped with it. Another voice said his name. “Gabriel. Stop looking for your sister. Come get me.” He brought the phone close enough for the glass to touch his cheek. His mother had been dead for fifteen years. “Mami?” The message repeated. The same breath, the same faint scrape before his name. He listened three times before he remembered how to end a call. He called Inés back. No answer.

passages.text: Download the blank release worksheet (.txt) From gameplay to a clear portfolio A website visitors can trust Worked example • fictional project From gameplay to a clear portfolio Start with one viewer question A portfolio clip needs a clear editorial purpose before it needs decoration. passages.title: Workshop guide | DTRT Lab
passages.text: Make one decision visible Choose the cut, crop, or label that helps someone follow that specific change on screen. Define a useful result A finished example should show the decision clearly enough for someone to explain your reasoning. See the worked diagram ORIGINAL WORKSHOP DIAGRAM Start with one viewer question 01 Question 02 Evidence 03 Decision 04 Result 4 / 4 decisions visible STEP 4 / 4 Inspect the material first Inspect duration, framing, repetition, and sound before designing the chapter.

passages.title: Workshop guide | DTRT Lab
passages.text: Measure the originals The three supplied edits measure fifteen point seven, fifteen point four five, and fifteen point nine five seconds. Check the frame All three source files use a portrait canvas with an overview and a larger detail view. Remove repeated action Their opening previews repeat later action; those previews and the first edit’s slowed replay are removed here. Separate sound from permission These workshop excerpts contain no audio stream; soundtrack permission is not inferred from possession of a file.

passages.title: Workshop guide | DTRT Lab
passages.text: See the worked diagram ORIGINAL WORKSHOP DIAGRAM Inspect the material first 1 15.700s source 2 15.450s source 3 15.950s source 4 Audio removed STEP 4 / 4 Build a beat map Use precise beats as an editing plan, then adjust them to the actual action. Sketch twelve seconds This twelve second timeline is an original planning illustration, not a measurement of the next clip. Give the setup a job Reserve three seconds to establish where attention belongs, then remove information that does not support it.

passages.title: Workshop guide | DTRT Lab
passages.text: Let the action develop Place the meaningful change between three and eight point five seconds, with its spatial context intact. Keep the result readable Use the remaining three point five seconds to make the consequence legible before the viewer leaves.
